content: Hypomenorrhea, also referred to as hypomenorrhoea, scanty periods, or spotting during menstruation, is characterized by an abnormally light menstrual blood flow. This condition is the opposite of hypermenorrhea, which is more accurately termed menorrhagia and involves excessive menstrual bleeding. One potential cause of hypomenorrhea is Asherman's syndrome, a condition involving intrauterine adhesions. In cases of Asherman's syndrome, hypomenorrhea or even amenorrhea (the absence of menstruation) may be the only noticeable clinical manifestation. The severity of menstrual deficiency in such cases is directly related to the extent of the intrauterine adhesions.
